questions.question: Where should the patched connector live? I'll need a durable home for ~6-10 patch commits and a pinned version that the service runs from.

options.label: GitHub fork (Recommended)
options.description: Fork qingzhu521/openchamber-pi-connector to your account, clone to ~/git/openchamber-pi-connector, work on a branch, service pins a commit. Generic fixes (agent-dir env, approvals) also offered upstream as PRs.

options.label: Local clone only
options.description: Same clone at ~/git/openchamber-pi-connector with local commits, no remote fork. Simpler, but no off-machine backup and no upstream PRs.

options.label: Upstream PRs, then pin
options.description: Only send PRs upstream and wait for merges before deploying. Cleanest long-term, but blocks deployment on a single maintainer.

questions.question: How should the new OpenChamber+OmO instance be deployed and exposed on the LAN? Paseo stays up on 6767 until the soak passes either way.

options.label: New unit on :4096 (Recommended)
options.description: New openchamber-omo.service on 127.0.0.1:4096 with its own data dir (~/.config/openchamber-omo) and UI password; add a 192.168.1.212:4096 portproxy + scheduled task + Domain/Private firewall rule (one UAC click). Old openchamber.service and its data stay untouched.

options.label: Reuse main OpenChamber
options.description: Point the existing ~/.config/openchamber profile and openchamber.service at the connector. Keeps your OpenChamber settings/projects, but its OpenCode sessions disappear from view and rollback means editing that profile back.

options.label: Take over 6767 later
options.description: Run on a localhost port during soak, then swap it onto 192.168.1.212:6767 when Paseo is retired. No new Windows rules, but no LAN access until cutover.

questions.question: OpenCode's revert undoes both the conversation and the file changes since a message. OmO has session-tree branching but no file snapshots. What should revert do?

options.label: Conversation + files (Recommended)
options.description: Connector snapshots the git working tree before each user turn (dangling `git stash create` commit refs, no branch/stash pollution) and on revert restores files + branches the OmO session back to before that message; unrevert restores the post-turn snapshot. Non-git dirs: conversation-only with a visible notice.

options.label: Conversation only
options.description: Revert branches the OmO session back to before the message; files are left as they are, with a clear notice in the UI that file changes were not undone.

options.label: Keep disabled
options.description: Revert/unrevert stay unavailable and return a clear error; use fork instead.
